cleared.check: Task 3 (L-914): compiler fixes in go1.25.6 to go1.25.13 and go1.26.0 to go1.26.11. The release page names only the packages, so every commit between consecutive tags was read from the release branch log of go.googlesource.com (20 ranges, 71 commits that touch cmd/compile, cmd/link or cmd/internal/obj).
cleared.result: Miscompilations on amd64 or arm64, by shape: #76967 constant facts propagated through an out-of-range jump table index (go1.25.6); #77253 static array initialisation that stores a stack pointer in a global (go1.25.8, go1.26.1); #77618 64-bit AND/OR constant folded into a sign-extended 32-bit immediate, seen in strings.HasSuffix (go1.26.1, amd64); #77623 regalloc clobbers one register twice when both inputs share it, shown by *y = *x with y the same pointer (go1.26.1); CVE-2026-27143 loop bounds check elimination with a negative or non-unit step (go1.25.9, go1.26.2); CVE-2026-27144 overlap detection misses a no-op interface conversion on the right side of an assignment (go1.25.9, go1.26.2); #78404 devirtualisation, now comparing types by pointer identity (go1.26.3); #79182 (x + x) << 63 or << 31 rewritten to x << 0 on amd64 (go1.25.11, go1.26.4); #80517 prove learns a fact before it holds and drops a bounds check, #79874 32-bit slice mask for a 64-bit slice (go1.25.13, go1.26.6); stack slot merging with a copied address (go1.25.13, go1.26.6); #81689 and #81668 stack-allocated slice backing store kept after a range or an &s[i].f escape (go1.26.9); #81863 dead store through a CondSelect (go1.26.11, F-117); #81868 the canonical Const64 amount of a narrow shift got the narrow type (go1.26.11, 'confirmed crashes, maybe misscompilations'). The other compiler fixes are crashes, hangs or build errors (regalloc loop, zero-sized values, write barrier, race instrumentation, PCALIGN loop, rotate amounts on 32-bit targets, DWARF heapaddr), other architectures (riscv64 sign extension, mips HI/LO and offsets, PPC64 atomics, arm32 and s390x merge locals), or cgo and linker hardening. bor v2.11.1, BNB Chain geth v1.8.2 and avalanchego 1.15.3 report go1.26.10, which holds every fix up to go1.26.10; what it lacks is #81863 and #81868 (and the open #82839).

cleared.check: Task 3: the shapes of #81868 (C1: an 8, 16 or 32 bit value shifted by a constant), #79182 (C2: shift left by 63 or 31, flagged when the operand is x + x, x * 2 or x << 1) and #81689/#81668 (C3: make of a slice with a non-constant length) added to the cycle 18 shapescan and run over holiman/uint256 v1.3.2 and v1.2.4 and the core/vm, core/state, core/types, trie, rlp and common/math trees of bor v2.11.1, bsc v1.8.2, coreth and graft/evm of avalanchego 1.15.3, libevm d398bc4dbe41, nitro geth 0e44603 and Celo op-geth c7ed55b8. A positive control file with the issue 79182 reproducer gives C1, C2 (dbl=true) and C3.
cleared.result: uint256 has no C1 site; its only C2 sites are Sqrt (v1.3.2 uint256.go:1335-1337, v1.2.4 1322-1326), z2[i] << 63 of a word that is not doubled, and no opcode calls Sqrt. The only C1 site in core/vm of every tree is BitVec.setN (bor core/vm/analysis_legacy.go:41, bsc :40, libevm analysis.go:40): byte(a >> 8) of a uint16, which marks the push data bits of PUSH2 to PUSH16 for jump destination analysis. Its shift amount is an untyped constant, which the SSA builder gives a 64-bit operand, while the faulty rule rewrote 8, 16 and 32 bit amounts; this was not checked in compiler output. It was tested on chain: for PUSH2 to PUSH16 at all eight alignments, a program jumps to each 0x5b byte inside and around the push data (1,620 cases, 1,080 of them must fail). Polygon (five bor v2.11.1 go1.26.10 builds), BNB Chain (Geth v1.8.2 go1.26.10, two builds), Avalanche (avalanchego 1.15.3 go1.26.10) and Ethereum (reth v2.11.0, control) give the specified outcome on all 1,620. The other C1 sites are bloom9, trie nibble encoding and the OP Stack FastLZ cost estimate, none on the path of a PoolManager opcode. C3 sites in core/vm (Memory.Resize and GetCopy, makeLog, codeBitmap, precompile inputs) build slices that are stored or returned whole; the three go1.26.10 builds already carry the #81689 and #81668 fixes.

leads.question: Does go1.26.10 apply the generic shift canonicalisation of Go issue 81868 to BitVec.setN or to any shift in holiman/uint256 and core/vm, as seen in the SSA dump (GOSSAFUNC) of a build from the go1.26.10 source archive?
leads.why: The rule rewrote shift amounts of 8, 16 and 32 bits; setN shifts a uint16 by a constant inside jump destination analysis. The on-chain test passes on 1,620 cases, but the compiled form was not read.

leads.question: Add a rule to the shared tools that refuses past-block state reads through rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm, rpc.hypurrscan.io and rpc.hyperlend.finance, and check the cycle 20 HyperEVM unit's scripts against it.
leads.why: Two of these endpoints always answer past-block state from head and the third does so on some requests, which turns a replay into a comparison with the wrong state.

leadResults.answer: The official endpoint and hypurrscan answer eth_call, eth_getStorageAt, eth_getBalance and eth_getCode at any past block with head state; purroofgroup and drpc honour the tag; hyperlend mixes a tag-honouring reth with official-client backends. No chain 999 clearance of cycles 9 to 19 read past-block state from the official endpoint or hypurrscan, and the one that used hyperlend (cycle 13 swap residuals) can only have been made harder to pass and was repeated on purroofgroup. Nothing must be rerun.

forno's op-geth backend follows the canonical chain: 606 heights from 75,046,581 on give the same hashes as celo-reth, and its head is within two blocks of reth's. forno splits 25 element batches across backends but not three element ones. The battery and targeted set were rerun with every chunk answered by each backend in a pinned three element batch, with no mismatch. Past-block reads are answered by celo-reth only, so the cycle 18 historical results came from the producing client. The unpinned Celo results of cycles 16 to 19 are listed; the script sets remain unpinned. shapescan over op-geth c7ed55b8 with the two missing core/vm and core/state files added finds no new site.

The fix lists were read from the release branch logs at go.googlesource.com. For the go1.26.10 builds of bor, BNB Chain geth and avalanchego the only unfixed miscompile shapes are issues 81863 (F-117), 81868 and the open 82839. The 81868 shape occurs in core/vm only in BitVec.setN, which passes 1,620 jump destination cases on all three networks; uint256 has no 81868 site and its only shift-by-63 sites are in Sqrt, which no opcode calls.
